name: Drawer
purpose: Present a finished modal side sheet while Atom owns focus, dismissal, portal, scroll-lock, and labeling behavior.
useWhen: A temporary modal task or navigation panel should enter from a screen edge.

avoidWhen.condition: The side region is persistent layout or the overlay has no edge meaning.

composition: Compose Trigger and Portal with sibling Overlay and Positioner; place Content inside Positioner. Use Header, Title, Body, Footer and authored CloseButton. Context supplies open/setOpen without another state owner.

Title is a native heading rather than a polymorphic layout host. Use its as prop to choose the heading level; do not pass a multi-element brand or layout through asChild. When the surface intentionally has no visible heading, give Content an explicit accessible name such as aria-label="Mobile navigation".

rules.statement: Use the shared token-only radius contract only on the public parts listed in docs/guides/radius.md. Omit it to retain the owner default; do not combine it with legacy corner shape or forward it to native elements. Core names and semantic roles are distinct; popup boundaries are independent of their triggers.
Use Drawer parts rather than hand-building overlay, focus trap, Escape, outside interaction, or portal behavior.
Give Content an accessible name with a concise Title or, when no visible heading is appropriate, an explicit aria-label or aria-labelledby on Content.
Choose size and placement from content needs: use xl when content may need the viewport but should shrink when short, and full only when the surface must always fill it.
Let top and bottom Drawers grow naturally to their selected size cap; keep long overflow in Drawer.Body instead of forcing a fixed application height.
Use Footer justify for simple action distribution, a Brick layout component inside Footer for complex grouping, and Button fullWidth only when the action itself should fill the row.
In React Server Components, import the component subpath as import * as Drawer from @flowstack-ui/brick/drawer; use the legacy root-package runtime object only inside a client-owned module.
Load styles.css or core.css plus drawer.css.

Use Positioner inset for offset panels. For container geometry pair absolute Positioner and Overlay inside a positioned region; Portal alone does not contain geometry. Container geometry does not scope document modality.
Size and placement accept sparse ResponsiveValue with xs/end defaults. Use CSS-only responsive values on one Content tree. Choose full only when the whole available region must fill.

Nonmodal is opt-in via modal=false. Omit Overlay; Positioner leaves its empty area pointer-transparent. trapFocus and preventScroll default to modal. Use cancelable Escape/outside events rather than rebuilding dismissal.

commonMistakes.mistake: Building a mobile menu as an absolutely positioned div or placing Close outside the labeled content hierarchy.
commonMistakes.correction: Use Drawer anatomy and compose the menu content with Brick navigation and layout components.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding use client to an entire Next page only to dereference the legacy Drawer runtime object.
commonMistakes.correction: Use the RSC-safe module-namespace subpath so only Drawer remains client-owned.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using asChild on Title or treating a brand lockup as a heading.
commonMistakes.correction: Keep branding in the visual header and name Content explicitly when there is no concise visible title.

validation: Test labeling, initial focus, focus containment/return, Escape, overlay, Close, scroll lock, content growth and capped Body overflow, touch, reduced motion, narrow screens, and nested portals.
Confirm CSS and every composed child component stylesheet are loaded.
In a React Server Component consumer, confirm the module-namespace form passes a production prerender without promoting the page to use client.
Verify retained DOM/input state, Context actions, responsive edges, container bounds, nonmodal background interaction, cancelable dismissal and named documentation parts.
